- When sentiment is positive (≥ 0.5) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly.
- When sentiment is negative (≤ -0.5), model often underestimates; adjust upward, especially if recent price is falling.
- Model frequently overshoots after sharp price spikes (e.g., +10%+ in 3-5 days), especially if sentiment was bullish; cap forecast at 10-15% above recent peak.
- If sentiment shifts from bullish to bearish mid-horizon, model often fails to adjust; reduce forecast slope or add early mean-reversion bias.
- For 30-day forecasts, model tends to overreact to short-term sentiment swings; apply smoothing or lagged sentiment weighting (e.g., 7-day sentiment average).
- If recent 3-5 day price is trending down, model often forecasts further decline; add upward bias if sentiment is neutral or slightly bullish.
- Model underestimates when sentiment is mixed or neutral; increase forecast by 2-5% if sentiment is 0.0–0.3 over last 5 days.
- Avoid forecasting below 70% of recent 10-day average unless sentiment is strongly bearish; use as floor for conservative models.
